conviction_note: Mixed evidence, no company-level number the market has not seen: a strong peer read-through (Alibaba Cloud accelerated to +53%, reported 2026-11-19) and an H2-weighted enterprise pipeline against a 14.4-vol-point downside skew, a fresh US remote-access chip rule and an unfunded H2 capex plan; findings sum to +0.9, the scaled number is (2*0.51-1)*9 = +0.18 because p_up sits at 51 given the skew, and abs_move is set well above the 5.3% event-implied number because the options are thin (OI 2,538, ATM spread 29% of mid), realised vol is 85% annualised and the last print moved about +10.6% intraday.
bar: Street consensus Q3 2026 revenue about US$492.8m (~+42% YoY in USD; roughly RMB3.3-3.4bn, ~+35% YoY in RMB and ~+9% QoQ from Q2's RMB3,072m), EPS -$0.04 per ADS, Earnings Whisper -$0.03; ONE source only (Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 2026-11-16, https://finviz.com/news/423372/kingsoft-clouds-first-operating-profit-faces-its-real-test-after-a-38-stock-slide). The company gives no formal quarterly guidance (Q2 release https://finviz.com/news/383528/kingsoft-cloud-announces-unaudited-second-quarter-2026-financial-results has only safe-harbor language). Not two agreeing sources and no company guide, so every finding is capped small. My own trajectory check (AI billings Q1 ~RMB1.0bn -> Q2 RMB1,327m; enterprise cloud Q3 2025 ~RMB726m, H2-weighted) lands around RMB3.28-3.34bn, i.e. at or slightly under the bar.
positioning_check: Short interest: about 7.9m ADS short, 5.8 days to cover at the FINRA 2026-09-30 settlement (Curved Trading, via search snippet https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/kc/short-interest/, page itself 403); Equibles early October 2026: 6.2m short, 2.1% of float, 5.6 days, rising (https://equibles.com/stocks/kc/shortinterest). Borrow fee 9.5% (curvedtrading snippet, undated). No November settlement found. Not a crowded short. Skew: 25-delta put minus call +14.43 vol points = downside paid; put/call OI 0.26; total OI only 2,538 contracts and ATM spread 28.6% of mid, so the chain is thin. Tape: -10.84% over 5 days, -29.39% over 20 days, -66% from the 52-week high, +12% off the 52-week low; the HK line (3896) fell -11.48% on 11-17 (BIS rule), -6.29% on 11-19, -7.16% on 11-20 and rose +2.30% on 11-23 (https://stockanalysis.com/quote/hkg/3896/history/).

findings.finding: Alibaba, the largest Chinese cloud peer, reported on 2026-11-19 (after KC last spoke on 2026-08-19) that AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue grew 53% YoY in the September quarter, accelerating from 45% in the June quarter, with external-customer revenue +64% and recurring external revenue +67%; KC's consensus already assumes ~+35% RMB / ~+42% USD growth, so the peer read is supportive of demand but does not by itself say KC clears the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: KC rose about +10.6% intraday on 2026-08-19 when Q2 revenue beat by ~$5m and AI billings grew 82% (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/why-kingsoft-cloud-stock-is-soaring-today/); no record of KC moving on a peer print.
findings.why_not_priced: KC's HK line fell -6.29% and -7.16% on 11-19 and 11-20, the sessions around the Alibaba print, while BABA itself rose ~7%; if the market had carried the peer's demand acceleration to KC, KC would not have made new lows into its own print. Peer read is a proxy: Alibaba's growth includes self-built chips and scale KC lacks, so sized small.
findings.independence: Compute pricing evidence (TrendForce 2026-11-19, GPU rental rates climbing; spring 2026 price hikes by Alibaba/Baidu/Tencent clouds) points the same way: https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/04/10/news-ai-compute-prices-rise-across-china-tencent-joins-alibaba-baidu-in-hikes-zhipu-raises-prices-again/ . Different document from the Alibaba release.

findings.finding: The US BIS interim final rule 'Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors' (issued 2026-11-16, effective 2026-11-19) requires licences for advanced chips going to data centres anywhere that provide >12m TPP of compute to China-headquartered firms, closing the overseas GPU-rental route; KC's HK shares fell -11.48% on 2026-11-17, the worst of the HK AI names that day, and the 11-24 call is the first chance for management to say how much of its AI capacity or GPU supply this touches.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the rule itself KC fell -8.13% intraday / -11.48% close in HK on 2026-11-17 (https://wap.stockstar.com/detail/IG2026111700011620). Management said on the Q2 call that constrained AI chip supply is a long-term condition and it is diversifying to domestic chips (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262118921-tradingkey).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock already fell ~11% on the day and kept falling. What is not priced is KC's own exposure number, which no source carries; I found no disclosure of KC renting overseas GPU capacity. Either a 'no material exposure' line (relief) or an AI-billings slowdown blamed on supply (further drop) could come on the call, so sized near zero with a wide band.
findings.independence: HK market report quoting the -8.13% move and the rule details: https://wap.stockstar.com/detail/IG2026111700011620 ; legal summaries of scope: https://www.gtlaw.com/de/insights/2026/11/bis-interim-final-rule-targets-remote-access-to-advanced-semiconductors-rescinds-ai-diffusion-rule . Same underlying rule, so one finding.

findings.finding: Enterprise cloud (23% of Q2 revenue, RMB714m, -1.3% YoY) was weak in Q2 because memory and storage price spikes delayed government budgets and project revenue was reclassified; on the Q2 call management said delivery and revenue recognition concentrate in H2 and 'we have actually quite a strong pipeline to deliver in the second half', and Q3 2025 enterprise revenue was only ~RMB726m (total RMB2,478m less public RMB1,752m), so an easy comparison sits under the Q3 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 enterprise decline was absorbed in a +10.6% day because public/AI cloud beat; in Q3 2025 the stock fell on a revenue miss (https://www.itiger.com/news/1179138488, a low-quality automated note whose figures partly mix in the parent's).
findings.why_not_priced: Every preview quotes the -1% enterprise decline as a concern (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-16) and none credits the H2 pipeline statement; if the market believed the rebound it would not frame enterprise as a risk. Net of the rest: public cloud (77%) still has to grow ~8-10% QoQ for the total to clear the bar, and the memory-price problem that delayed budgets has not visibly eased (Xiaomi warned of rising memory costs), so sized small.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 segment base from the Q3 2025 release: https://finviz.com/news/233576/kingsoft-cloud-announces-unaudited-third-quarter-2025-financial-results . Management's H2 statement and the Q2 numbers share the Q2 documents.

findings.finding: Cash fell to RMB4,674m at 2026-06-30 from RMB6,018m at year end, borrowings were ~RMB6,681m, and management held full-year capex at ~RMB15bn after ~RMB6.2bn in H1, leaving ~RMB8.8bn for H2 against ~RMB1.1bn a quarter of adjusted EBITDA; the last equity raise (Sep 2025, HK$2.8bn at HK$8.29) came a month after a results print, and the HK shares now trade at HK$3.12.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: KC fell after pricing the Sep 2025 placement (https://ng.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/kingsoft-cloud-stock-falls-after-pricing-hk28-billion-share-offering-93CH-2115703); the Q2 2026 print with the cash decline still rose ~10.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: The gap is in the public record and previews mention capex and borrowing costs, so partly priced. The question was asked: the money buys AI capacity against AI billings +82% YoY and related-party caps with Xiaomi/Kingsoft raised to RMB10bn a year, so it funds visible demand; that pulls the sign toward zero. What stays negative is the price: any equity funding at HK$3 is roughly 2.7x as dilutive per dollar as the 2025 placement, and the Q3 cash walk and capex commentary land on the call. No placement, CB or loan was found for 2026.
findings.independence: Q2 call: full-year capex base case unchanged, related-party caps raised (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262118921-tradingkey). Same company documents, so one finding.

findings.finding: GPU rental and AI compute prices in China kept rising through 2026: the big clouds raised AI compute prices 5-34% in spring, H100 rentals in China rose 20-30% by April, and TrendForce reported on 2026-11-19 that Nvidia GPU rental rates are still climbing; for KC, whose AI billings are 56% of public cloud, this supports price per unit but also raises server cost and capex.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: KC's adjusted gross margin went from 12.8% (Q1 2026) to 15.4% (Q2 2026) and the stock rose on Q2; no line-specific reaction history on pricing.
findings.why_not_priced: Industry series, public for months, so mostly priced; KC has not confirmed its own price changes, so this is macro-to-company transmission and sized small. If the market priced margin upside, previews would not frame gross margin as the open question ('investors want to see the margin expansion', briefglance preview 2026-10-29).
findings.independence: Caixin on rationing and price hikes: https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-04-21/computing-shortage-forces-chinese-ai-firms-to-ration-services-102436452.html . Shares the demand theme with the Alibaba finding but is a different series (price, not volume).

findings.finding: Ecosystem demand cuts both ways: shareholders approved raising the connected-transaction caps with Xiaomi and Kingsoft to RMB10bn for each of 2026 and 2027, and Q2 ecosystem revenue was RMB810m (+28% YoY, 26% of revenue), while Xiaomi, the largest related customer, posted its third straight profit decline in Q2 2026 (adjusted net income about -43%) on the memory-cost squeeze; Xiaomi's own Q3 2026 results were not found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none found for this line specifically.
findings.why_not_priced: Both halves are public and offset; filed so the judges see them. If Xiaomi had cut AI spending, KC's ecosystem line would show it on 11-24, but nothing dated in the window says so.
findings.independence: Xiaomi Q2 2026 profit decline: https://thenextweb.com/news/xiaomi-q2-2026-earnings-memory-crunch . The cap increase also appears in the April 2026 HKEX circular via https://www.panabee.com/news/kingsoft-cloud-earnings-q3-2026 (AI-generated summary).

findings.finding: Into the print the ADS is -29.4% over 20 sessions and -66% from its 52-week high (HK: HK$4.68 on 11-05 to HK$3.12 on 11-23), sentiment has gone from 53% bullish before Q2 to slightly bearish (Earnings Whispers), and CICC still has a US$20 target; the last print with a beat produced about +10.6%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: +10.6% intraday on the Q2 2026 beat (2026-08-19); -2.7% to -3.8% after the Q1 2026 miss (low-quality automated reports, e.g. https://www.lbsim.ac.in/expert-time/KC-Q1-2026-Earnings-EPS-Misses-Expectations-by-Over-40-Stock-Slides-27-30-6347).
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so by definition it is what the market already did; the 14.4-point downside skew says options buyers still want protection after the slide. Filed near zero: a washed-out tape lowers the bar for a relief move but is not evidence of what the print says.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers sentiment and slide: https://finviz.com/news/423372/kingsoft-clouds-first-operating-profit-faces-its-real-test-after-a-38-stock-slide ; CICC target cited in https://stock.10jqka.com.cn/20261102/c681346270.shtml (promotional repost).

outside_window.finding: BIS remote-access IFR comment period runs to about 2027-01-18 and a final rule is expected later; any change to scope resolves after the exit.

Q3 2026 company guidance: none exists; the Q2 release has no outlook
Second independent consensus source (chartmill 403; nothing else found)
VNET Q3 2026 (reported 2026-11-23, revenue +14.8%) and GDS (reports 2026-11-25): data-centre peers, not judged relevant to KC's cloud revenue line

baseline_tension: The positive peer and pipeline evidence cuts against the +14.4 vol-point put skew and a -29% 20-day run-up; the negatives I found (BIS rule, funding gap) are the ones the price already shows, so the net is close to balanced and p_up sits at 51.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar from one source, no company guide): checked that every finding is already small; nothing above 0.6 survives.
Rule 5 (proxy sized below company documents): Alibaba peer finding cut from +0.8 to +0.6.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the money funds AI capacity against +82% AI billings, so the funding-gap finding moved from -0.8 to -0.3; only the dilution-at-a-low-price part stays negative.

Rule 5/7 (an unexplained drawdown and positioning are worth about 0; respect the skew): added the run-up/positioning item as its own finding at +0.1 rather than letting it lean the day, and lowered p_up from 52 to 51 because the positive lean runs against a 14.4-point downside skew.
Rule 8 and the core's 'sizes are too small': abs_move_pct kept at 9.0, well above the 5.3% event-implied move, because the chain is thin and the last print moved ~10.6%.
